text: They say there's a reef east of Saltmarrow where the fish swim in circles round a sunken bell. Probably nonsense.
A fisherman from Mariner's Rest swears he hooked something golden and longer than his boat, way out past the charts. Lost the rod.
Ironwatch doubled the guns on the north wall. Either the Commodore knows something, or he's bored.
Raven's Landing sells rum without the Crown's stamp. Cheaper, and the hangover's free.
Somebody in Kingsport bought every map of the Forgotten Keys they could find. Paid in gold. Didn't haggle.
There's a crocodile in Serpent's Hollow they call Old Gnasher. Big as a longboat, they say, and twice as patient.
The monks on Saint Vesper ring their bell at dusk, every dusk, for every ship that never came home.
Stormbreak's regatta record keeps changing hands. The Regatta Master says the stacks shift when no one's looking.
Prices on silk in Saltmarrow are through the roof. Somebody's making a fortune hauling it from Kingsport.
The Deep Seam on Goldwater goes down further than anyone's dared. The foreman pays well for brave fools.
Haven't seen a merchant convoy in a week. Either the trade's dried up or someone's been eating them.
On Whispering Key a woman in grey walks the mansion halls. The medium says she's waiting for someone.
A whale-sized shadow followed a sloop out of Crooked Reef. The crew swore off rum for a month. Two days, really.
The Tidewatch has a frigate that's never lost a fight. Admiral Galloway's own. Nobody's told her it's bad luck to say so.
If a patrol hails you with a hold full of untaxed rum, the smugglers' advice is simple: don't be there in fifteen seconds.
Bayou folk at Hookline say the alligators know the names of everyone who's drowned in the Mirefen.
They say a whole city lies under the sea, south and west. Vesh Amaru. Divers come back with paintings and stories they won't finish.
Bounty hunters were asking after you. Well, not you. Someone who looked like you. Probably.
There's a tournament in Saltmarrow. Five waves, and the champion takes the purse.
Mind the whirlpools. The Drain nearly had my cousin. He's still dizzy.
A peddler's been seen in the ports. Sells rings that make you lucky. Or so she says.
There's an old man on the beaches at night. Hums a song. If you can see him, you're one of the lucky ones.
Rumour is there's a price on your head, {player}. Not that I'd ever mention it to a marine.
There are posters with your face on them in Ironwatch. Not a good likeness. Flattering, really.
The Drowned Bell's been tolling every night this month. Every toll, another crew comes up out of the sea.
They say the old bellfounder still lives on Ashfall. Tamsin, was it? Nobody's seen her in town for years.
Somebody's poking about the Sunken Reach belltower. Brave, or stupid.
Ashfall's smugglers have a forge in the hills. They say they found something in the rock that glows.
Word is someone's had a new bell cast. To silence the old one, they say. Good luck to them.
The Drowned Bell's quiet. Has been since Captain Thorne went down. I owe somebody a drink for that.
Since the bell stopped, the fishing's come back to Driftwood. My cousin's never been happier.
There's talk of seven old stones, and every captain in the Reach suddenly wanting them.
Rook Varga's calling every free captain to Blackthorn. Calls it an Accord. I call it Rook wanting more ships.
The Lantern Court? Never heard of it. And if you're smart, neither have you.
Folk at the Last Horizon say the gate on the summit's started to hum.
Since the gate shut, the ghost ships have thinned out. You'd know something about that, I hear.
The cursed stopped coming ashore in the towns. Some say a Warden sealed something at the edge of the chart.
The drowned won't touch a certain captain, they say. Some say that captain's the worst thing in the sea now.
The Tidewatch has a new name at the top of their list. A Sovereign, of all things.
There are lanterns burning on the Horizon Gate every night now. Nobody says who lights them.
Governor Harrow's in a fine mood lately. That never bodes well for anyone else.
Somebody opened the Horizon Gate. You can see the light from the Keys on a clear night.
Storms like this wash things up. Old things. Last big blow, a chest of First Tide coins came ashore at the Keys.
At night, if you sail past Hollowgrave, you can still hear singing under the water.
Night like this, the Sovereign Dawn's supposed to rise over Crooked Reef. Lost with every hand, forty years back.
The Shattered Reach. A hundred islands, give or take, and every one of them with a story nobody tells straight.
The Tidewatch holds the forts, the Brethren hold the harbours, the smugglers hold whatever's left, and the sea holds everyone.
The Navy. Blue coats, big guns, Ironwatch and Crownwatch and every fort between. Commodore Vey runs the patrols; Admiral Galloway runs Commodore Vey.
Stay on their good side and they'll pay you to sink ghost ships. Cross them and they'll hang a poster with your face on it.
The Saltmarrow Brethren. Pirates with articles and a vote. Mags Tallow keeps their book at the Saltmarrow tavern.
They don't love the Navy, they don't love the cursed, and they love a full purse more than either.
Raven's Landing. Isadora Vance's people. Untaxed rum, powder without papers, and stranger cargo besides.
If you can outrun a patrol, there's good money in their crates. If you can't, there's a long rope at Ironwatch.
The dead don't stay down in the Reach. Ghost ships, cursed crews coming ashore on moonless nights, things in the deep water.
Some blame the Drowned Bell. The old folk say it's older than any bell: something the First Tide did, before the sea took them.
The Drowned Bell's quiet now, thanks to somebody. But the dead still walk some nights.
The old folk say the bell was just the loudest part of it. That the rest is older, out past the charts.
Quieter than it's been in my lifetime. They say a Warden shut a gate at the edge of the world.
